title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
A self-driving car in autonomous mode struck and killed a duck in a Austin neighborhood. A human safety operator was present in the vehicle but did not intervene to prevent the collision. The system failed to detect or avoid the animal, which was nesting in a location frequented by pedestrians and vehicles.

This is a failure in object detection and collision avoidance during normal deployment. The autonomous vehicle did not recognize the duck as an obstacle requiring the car to slow or stop, despite the animal being stationary and in the roadway. It would have taken either more robust detection of small animals in the car's environment, or a human operator attentive enough to override the system before impact occurred.

It is not established whether the vehicle's failure to stop at a stop sign, which residents alleged, was responsible for the collision.

Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An Avride autonomous vehicle operating in Austin, Texas struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood, causing significant community backlash. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck was nesting in a pot outside a local restaurant, and residents had grown attached to it, adding to their concern about autonomous vehicle safety in their area.

Avride confirmed the vehicle was in autonomous mode during the incident and investigated the complaint that the car failed to stop at a stop sign, concluding no evidence supported this claim. The company has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets near the lake and is now running simulation experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations. Meanwhile, local residents recovered the duck's eggs and placed them in an incubator, and other autonomous vehicle companies continue testing in Austin.
